249	Definition le_cons (κa : kind) {Γ : list kind} {r : nat} (Hr : r <= length Γ) :
250	  S r <= length (κa :: Γ) := le_n_S r (length Γ) Hr.
251	
252	Fixpoint walk_inf (Γ : list kind) (κ0 : kind) (r : nat) (Hr : r <= length Γ)
253	    (arg : inf Γ κ0)
254	    (kap : forall (Γ' : list kind) (k1 k2 : kind),
255	        inf Γ' (k1 ⇒ k2) -> kind_cod (k1 ⇒ k2) κ0 -> inf Γ' k1 -> inf Γ' k2)
256	    {κd : kind} (t : inf (ins_at r κ0 Γ) κd) {struct t} : inf Γ κd
257	with walk_isp (Γ : list kind) (κ0 : kind) (r : nat) (Hr : r <= length Γ)
258	    (arg : inf Γ κ0)
259	    (kap : forall (Γ' : list kind) (k1 k2 : kind),
260	        inf Γ' (k1 ⇒ k2) -> kind_cod (k1 ⇒ k2) κ0 -> inf Γ' k1 -> inf Γ' k2)
261	    {κd : kind} (sp : isp (ins_at r κ0 Γ) κd) {struct sp} : iwalkres Γ κ0 κd
262	with walk_icon (Γ : list kind) (κ0 : kind) (r : nat) (Hr : r <= length Γ)
263	    (arg : inf Γ κ0)
264	    (kap : forall (Γ' : list kind) (k1 k2 : kind),
265	        inf Γ' (k1 ⇒ k2) -> kind_cod (k1 ⇒ k2) κ0 -> inf Γ' k1 -> inf Γ' k2)
266	    (x : icon (ins_at r κ0 Γ)) {struct x} : icon Γ.
267	Proof.
268	  - destruct t as [κa κr b | κ sp | x t | x t].
269	    + (* lam *)
270	      exact (@inf_lam Γ κa κr
271	        (@walk_inf (κa :: Γ) κ0 (S r) (le_cons κa Hr)
272	           (@shift_inf (κa :: nil) 0 Γ (Nat.le_0_l (length Γ)) κ0 arg)
273	           kap κr b)).
274	    + (* neutral *)
275	      exact (@iwalkres_inf Γ κ0 κ (@walk_isp Γ κ0 r Hr arg kap κ sp)).
276	    + (* carr *)
277	      exact (@inf_carr Γ (@walk_icon Γ κ0 r Hr arg kap x)
278	               (@walk_inf Γ κ0 r Hr arg kap ⋆ t)).
279	    + (* cprod *)
280	      exact (@inf_cprod Γ (@walk_icon Γ κ0 r Hr arg kap x)
281	               (@walk_inf Γ κ0 r Hr arg kap ⋆ t)).
282	  - destruct sp as [κ i H | κ x | κ c0 | κ1 κ2 sp a].
283	    + (* bvar *)
284	      destruct (Nat.eq_dec i r) as [Ei|Ei].
285	      * subst i.
286	        pose proof (nth_ins_target_kind r κ0 κ Γ Hr H) as Heq.
287	        exact (@iw_target Γ κ0 κ
288	                 (cast_inf (eq_sym Heq) arg)
289	                 (match Heq in (_ = z) return kind_cod κ z with
290	                  | eq_refl => kc_refl κ
291	                  end)).
292	      * destruct (lt_eq_lt_dec i r) as [[Hlt|Heq]|Hgt].
293	        -- exact (@iw_spine Γ κ0 κ
294	                   (@isp_bvar Γ κ i
295	                      (eq_trans (eq_sym (nth_error_ins_at_lt r i κ0 Γ Hlt Hr)) H))).
296	        -- subst i. exfalso. apply Ei. reflexivity.
297	        -- exact (@iw_spine Γ κ0 κ
298	                   (@isp_bvar Γ κ (i - 1)
299	                      (eq_trans (eq_sym (nth_error_ins_at_gt r i κ0 Γ Hgt Hr)) H))).
300	    + (* fvar *)
301	      exact (@iw_spine Γ κ0 κ (@isp_fvar Γ κ x)).
302	    + (* ctor *)
303	      exact (@iw_spine Γ κ0 κ (@isp_ctor Γ κ c0)).
304	    + (* app *)
305	      exact (@iwalkres_app Γ κ0 κ1 κ2 kap
306	               (@walk_isp Γ κ0 r Hr arg kap (κ1 ⇒ κ2) sp)
307	               (@walk_inf Γ κ0 r Hr arg kap κ1 a)).
308	  - destruct x as [κ a b]. exact (@icon_eq Γ κ
309	      (@walk_inf Γ κ0 r Hr arg kap κ a)
310	      (@walk_inf Γ κ0 r Hr arg kap κ b)).
311	Defined.
312	
313	Arguments walk_inf Γ κ0 r Hr arg kap {κd} t.
314	Arguments walk_isp Γ κ0 r Hr arg kap {κd} sp.
315	Arguments walk_icon Γ κ0 r Hr arg kap x.

401	Lemma iwalkres_app_spine {Γ : list kind} {κ0 κ1 κ2 : kind}
402	    (kap : forall (Γ' : list kind) (k1 k2 : kind),
403	        inf Γ' (k1 ⇒ k2) -> kind_cod (k1 ⇒ k2) κ0 -> inf Γ' k1 -> inf Γ' k2)
404	    (s : isp Γ (κ1 ⇒ κ2)) (a : inf Γ κ1) :
405	  @iwalkres_app Γ κ0 κ1 κ2 kap (iw_spine s) a = iw_spine (isp_app s a).
406	Proof. cbn [iwalkres_app]. reflexivity. Qed.

408	Lemma iwalkres_app_target {Γ : list kind} {κ0 κ1 κ2 : kind}
409	    (kap : forall (Γ' : list kind) (k1 k2 : kind),
410	        inf Γ' (k1 ⇒ k2) -> kind_cod (k1 ⇒ k2) κ0 -> inf Γ' k1 -> inf Γ' k2)
411	    (v : inf Γ (κ1 ⇒ κ2)) (H : kind_cod (κ1 ⇒ κ2) κ0) (a : inf Γ κ1) :
412	  @iwalkres_app Γ κ0 κ1 κ2 kap (iw_target v H) a =
413	  iw_target (kap Γ κ1 κ2 v H a) (kc_step H).
414	Proof. cbn [iwalkres_app]. reflexivity. Qed.

416	Lemma iwalkres_app_ext {Γ : list kind} {κ0 κ1 κ2 : kind}
417	    (kap1 kap2 : forall (Γ' : list kind) (k1 k2 : kind),
418	        inf Γ' (k1 ⇒ k2) -> kind_cod (k1 ⇒ k2) κ0 -> inf Γ' k1 -> inf Γ' k2)
419	    (Hk : forall (Γ' : list kind) (k1 k2 : kind) v H a,
420	        kap1 Γ' k1 k2 v H a = kap2 Γ' k1 k2 v H a)
421	    (r1 r2 : iwalkres Γ κ0 (κ1 ⇒ κ2)) (a1 a2 : inf Γ κ1) :
422	  r1 = r2 -> a1 = a2 ->
423	  @iwalkres_app Γ κ0 κ1 κ2 kap1 r1 a1 =
424	  @iwalkres_app Γ κ0 κ1 κ2 kap2 r2 a2.
425	Proof.
426	  intros Er Ea. subst r2. subst a2.
427	  dependent destruction r1.

Require Import Utf8.

Require Import Binding.Core.

Require Import Binding.Inc.

Require Import Binding.Properties.

Require Import Morphisms.

Record Ctx {V : Type} :=
  {dom : Set;
   arr :> dom -> V
  }.

Arguments Ctx V : clear implicits.

Definition mtC {V : Type} : Ctx V :=
  {| dom := Empty_set;
     arr x := match x with end
  |}.

Definition extC {V : Type} (v : V) (Γ : Ctx V) : Ctx V :=
  {| dom := inc (dom Γ);
     arr x := match x with
              | VZ => v
              | VS x => Γ x
              end
  |}.

Notation "'ε'" := mtC.

Notation "Γ ▹ v" := (extC v Γ) (at level 40, left associativity).

Class IntPureCore {V : Type} (F : V → Ctx V → Type) : Type :=
  int_pure : ∀ (Γ : Ctx V) v (x : dom Γ) (EQ : Γ x = v) , F v Γ.

Arguments int_pure {V F _ Γ}.

Record Arr {V : Type} {Γ Δ : Ctx V} : Type :=
  { apply_arr : dom Γ → dom Δ;
    arr_hom   : ∀ x : dom Γ, Δ (apply_arr x) = Γ x
  }.

Task: focus on the list-insertion commutation laws and then the context-indexed shift/walk theorem in `/workspace/NbeFork.v`.

Outcome: the two list-insertion commutation equalities are now fully proved. The generalized `shift_inf`/`walk_inf` theorem and `walk_app_inf` are not yet compiled, so I am not claiming A or C complete.

Compiled additions in `/workspace/NbeFork.v` (file compiles with `rocq c -R . Top NbeFork.v`; no `Admitted`/`admit`/`Abort`/axioms):

- `ins_at_app`:
  ```coq
  forall r κ A B,
    length A <= r ->
    ins_at r κ (A ++ B) = A ++ ins_at (r - length A) κ B
  ```
- `ins_at_length_prefix`:
  ```coq
  ins_at (length A) κ (A ++ B) = A ++ κ :: B
  ```
- `ins_list_at_app`:
  ```coq
  forall c d A B, length A = c ->
    ins_list_at c d (A ++ B) = A ++ d ++ B
  ```
- `app_cons_assoc`:
  ```coq
  A ++ a :: (C ++ D) = (A ++ a :: C) ++ D
  ```
- `ins_list_at_ins_at_lt`:
  ```coq
  forall c r d κ Γ,
    c < r -> r <= length Γ ->
    ins_list_at c d (ins_at r κ Γ)
    = ins_at (r + length d) κ (ins_list_at c d Γ)
  ```
- `ins_list_at_ins_at_ge`:
  ```coq
  forall c r d κ Γ,
    r <= c -> c <= length Γ ->
    ins_list_at (S c) d (ins_at r κ Γ)
    = ins_at r κ (ins_list_at c d Γ)
  ```
- `length_ins_list_at`:
  ```coq
  c <= length Γ ->
  length (ins_list_at c d Γ) = length Γ + length d
  ```
- `cast_ctx`, `cast_ctx_refl`, `cast_ctx_lam`, including distribution of a context cast under `inf_lam`.

The remaining obstruction for A is the cast coherence in the `inf_lam` branch of the walk-shift Fixpoint: the recursive body uses a context equality between
`ins_list_at (S c) d (ins_at (S r) κ0 (κa :: Γ))` and
`ins_at (S r + length d) κ0 (ins_list_at (S c) d (κa :: Γ))`,
while the outer walk uses the same equality transported under `cons κa`. Aligning these casts needs proof-irrelevance of list-context equality (decidable via `list_eq_dec kindEqDec.eq_dec`) or a cast-irrelevance lemma; currently only the positive list equalities and `cast_ctx_lam` are compiled.

B is structurally already handled: the target bvar kind is forced by `nth_ins_target_kind`, so the mismatch branch that broke the unindexed walker cannot occur.

No counterexample to the corrected indexed shift statement was found. C/D and the nil-consistency corollary remain open.

Since eval is on a closed-over-target nf where the binder is represented as a de Bruijn binder, we need nf bodies with binders.

Maybe use **nf with named binders too**: nf over a context of *kinds with atom type* could use all variables as atoms, and lambdas carry a binder atom with a freshness side-condition (locally nameless cofinite). This complicates.

Let's consider sticking with NbeFork's list-based contexts and free vars as nat, and handle arbitrary Δ by a **transport/renaming**: For a given Hstar instance Δ A B, the types A,B use finitely many variables, but also the tproves derivation H uses finitely many. We could avoid arbitrary Δ by a *logical relation over all Δ* but with nf contexts built as lists? Maybe use the fact that **Ctx kind is a small category and every Ctx is a quotient of a list context?** Not true for uncountable dom. But for the semantic soundness proof, we can interpret env over arbitrary dom Δ into nf values whose *free names are Δ atoms*; that's the locally nameless with fvar atoms, which NbeFork already almost has (fvar nat). The source context for eval is Δ atoms, and shift lemma needs source context commutation. But perhaps we can *define shift* differently: instead of `shift` (insert at front), define a **renaming-based embedding** `rename (f : dom Δ₁ -> typ?)`. Actually for the substitution lemma with tbind/liftS, we need shift (insert front). NbeFork's machinery with lists handles insertion positions, and we can adapt the same list insertion arithmetic to **target binder lists**; the source context mismatch is only in the shift lemma, where insertion under binders can be reorganized using the isomorphism extC κb (extC κa Δ) ≅ extC κa (extC κb Δ) at the level of *terms/values*? The term shift' is a term in extC κb (extC κa Δ₂). Its target evaluation context Γb = κb::κa::Γ. The IH shift lemma could be formulated not for shift-at-front but for **shift at arbitrary insertion position in the list of binders**, parameterized by list context. If free names are atoms from base Δ, source contexts built as `ctx_of_binders bs Δ` = nested extC. Insertion of a new binder can be at any position in bs. We need a shift lemma for all insertion positions. The proof is structural with careful list arithmetic (NbeFork did a lot of this). This might be feasible but heavy.

Let's step back and consider **avoiding the shift lemma by defining eval environments to be *substitutions* rather than nf values**, i.e., eval of types under an environment that maps source variables to *types* in a target context, and then normalize at the end? For the substitution lemma, the environment for Δ₂ is actually the substitution ρ itself; we could define eval with environments of nf but where the extension under a lambda maps the lambda binder to a **fresh free variable atom** that is *not* a binder, then abstract at the end. This is the "Kripke with atoms" approach: nf lambdas can be represented as `nf_lam (body over extC ka Γ)`; eval of t_lam under env maps VZ to eta_expand(sp_bvar 0), unavoidable.

OK, maybe we can simplify by **not proving the substitution lemma for arbitrary ρ**, and instead prove only the specific cases needed for tproves rules:
- tpi_beta: norm (subst τ σ) = appN (norm (ƛτ)) (norm σ) where subst uses mk_subst.
- tpi_lam/shift: rules produce terms shifted via `shift`/map; we need norm equality for lam bodies from IH, which is direct.
- tpi_eta: needs cancel lemma.
So we only need SL for ρ = mk_subst σ (single substitution) and for the shift lemma. Still the same t_lam case needing shift under binder. But perhaps for a *single* substitution, the shift of the argument σ under binders is `shift` and its evaluation under the extended env equals `weak`—same lemma.

Hmm.

Let's revisit the possibility of using **hereditary substitution directly on syntax with de Bruijn indices and proving norm/equality without environments**. The shift lemma is still needed for beta.

Wait—maybe there's a way to prove beta without a substitution lemma by defining `norm` via a **normalization function that is invariant by construction**, e.g., `norm` computes **βη-long normal form**, and beta is proven by **strong normalization of the *typing derivation***: the term `subst τ σ` has a normal form; but we need equality with app. Could use the **Church-Rosser theorem** plus a simple fact: appN(norm ƛτ, norm σ) is a reduct of both after substitution? No.

Let me look for an alternative mathematical characterization of the equational theory that is easy to prove sound for the rules. What if we interpret types into **hereditarily finite sets / trees with binding** where functions are *syntactic closures* and equality is *αβη-conversion*, and prove the tproves rules using **substitution lemmas for the syntactic calculus that are easy because closure-based**? That's NBE.

Perhaps we should just commit to the locally-nameless NBE and grind through. Before that, let's check if there are existing helpful lemmas in TaskPrefix for substitution/tbind and contexts that can reduce work: search for substitution lemmas, `subst_`, `tbind` lemmas.

=== SNFork ===
Require Import TaskPrefix.
Require Import Lang.FOmegaEq.Types Lang.FOmegaEq.Kinds Lang.FOmegaEq.Syntax Lang.FOmegaEq.Typing Lang.FOmegaEq.OpSemantics.
Require Import Binding.Intrinsic Binding.Lib Binding.Env.
Require Import Stdlib.Program.Equality.
Import Binding.Intrinsic (Ctx, dom, extC, Build_Ctx, mtC).
Import kindEqDec.
Local Open Scope typ_scope.

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* A minimal beta-reduction relation, used to state the SN/Tait target. *)
(* Constraints inside carr/cprod are treated opaquely: beta never steps
   inside a constraint, which is sound for the tdiscr model we need.     *)

Inductive bstep {Δ : Ctx kind} : forall {κ : kind}, typ κ Δ -> typ κ Δ -> Prop :=
| bstep_beta {κa κr : kind} (b : typ κr (extC κa Δ)) (a : typ κa Δ) :
    bstep ((t_lam b) a) (subst b a)
| bstep_app_l {κa κr : kind} {f f' : typ (κa ⇒ κr) Δ} (a : typ κa Δ) :
    bstep f f' -> bstep (f a) (f' a)
| bstep_app_r {κa κr : kind} (f : typ (κa ⇒ κr) Δ) {a a' : typ κa Δ} :
    bstep a a' -> bstep (f a) (f a')
| bstep_lam {κa κr : kind} {b b' : typ κr (extC κa Δ)} :
    bstep b b' -> bstep (t_lam b) (t_lam b')
| bstep_carr {ψ : constr Δ} {a a' : typ ⋆ Δ} :
    bstep a a' -> bstep (t_carr ψ a) (t_carr ψ a')
| bstep_cprod {ψ : constr Δ} {a a' : typ ⋆ Δ} :
    bstep a a' -> bstep (t_cprod ψ a) (t_cprod ψ a').

Definition SN {Δ : Ctx kind} {κ : kind} (τ : typ κ Δ) : Prop :=
  Acc (fun (x y : typ κ Δ) => @bstep Δ κ y x) τ.

Lemma SN_bstep {Δ : Ctx kind} {κ : kind} {τ τ' : typ κ Δ} :
  SN τ -> bstep τ τ' -> SN τ'.
Proof.
  intros H Hstep. destruct H as [Hacc]. apply Hacc. exact Hstep.
Qed.

(* The standard Tait candidate at base is SN.  Note: this alone does not
   separate constructor heads; it only gives termination. *)
Fixpoint Red {Δ : Ctx kind} (κ : kind) : typ κ Δ -> Prop :=
  match κ as k return typ k Δ -> Prop with
  | KTyp => fun τ => SN τ
  | KArr κa κr => fun τ => forall (a : typ κa Δ), Red κa a -> Red κr (τ a)
  end.

(* A few genuinely proved SN facts. *)
Lemma SN_ctor {Δ : Ctx kind} {κ : kind} (c : tctor κ) : SN (@t_ctor Δ κ c).
Proof.
  constructor. intros τ' Hstep. dependent destruction Hstep.
Qed.

Lemma SN_var {Δ : Ctx kind} {κ : kind} (x : dom Δ) (EQ : Δ x = κ) :
  SN (@t_var Δ κ x EQ).
Proof.
  constructor. intros τ' Hstep. dependent destruction Hstep.
Qed.

Lemma Red_ctor_star {Δ : Ctx kind} (c : tctor ⋆) : Red ⋆ (@t_ctor Δ ⋆ c).
Proof. apply SN_ctor. Qed.

Lemma Red_var_star {Δ : Ctx kind} (x : dom Δ) (EQ : Δ x = ⋆) :
  Red ⋆ (@t_var Δ ⋆ x EQ).
Proof. apply SN_var. Qed.

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* Exact equivalence of the base fact with HappR_star.                  *)

Lemma HappR_star_of_Hstar
  (Hstar : forall (Δ : Ctx kind) (A B : typ ⋆ Δ),
      nil ⊩ (A ≃ B) -> ⊮ (A ≃ B) -> False) :
  forall (Δ : Ctx kind) (κr κc : kind)
         (σ1 σ2 : typ (⋆ ⇒ κr) Δ) (c : tctor κc) (τ1 τ2 : typ ⋆ Δ),
    tctd σ1 c -> tctd σ2 c ->
    nil ⊩ (σ1 τ1) ≃ (σ2 τ2) -> ⊮ (τ1 ≃ τ2) -> False.
Proof.
  intros Δ κr κc σ1 σ2 c τ1 τ2 HI1 HI2 H HD.
  exact (Hstar Δ τ1 τ2 (tpi_appInjR HI1 HI2 H) HD).
Qed.

Lemma Hstar_of_HappR_star
  (HappR : forall (Δ : Ctx kind) (κr κc : kind)
      (σ1 σ2 : typ (⋆ ⇒ κr) Δ) (c : tctor κc) (τ1 τ2 : typ ⋆ Δ),
      tctd σ1 c -> tctd σ2 c ->
      nil ⊩ (σ1 τ1) ≃ (σ2 τ2) -> ⊮ (τ1 ≃ τ2) -> False) :
  forall (Δ : Ctx kind) (A B : typ ⋆ Δ),
    nil ⊩ (A ≃ B) -> ⊮ (A ≃ B) -> False.
Proof.
  intros Δ A B H HD.
  set (σ := @t_ctor Δ (⋆ ⇒ ⋆ ⇒ ⋆) tc_arr).
  assert (Happ : nil ⊩ (σ A) ≃ (σ B)).
  { eapply tpi_app. apply tpi_ctor. exact H. }
  eapply (HappR Δ (⋆ ⇒ ⋆) (⋆ ⇒ ⋆ ⇒ ⋆) σ σ tc_arr A B).
  - apply inj_ctor.
  - apply inj_ctor.
  - exact Happ.
  - exact HD.
Qed.

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
(* What a normalization/Tait model would have to provide.               *)
(* `nf` is intended to be a beta(-eta) normalizer.  The first obligation
   is soundness for nil tproves; the second is head separation, which SN
   alone (Red at base = SN) does NOT give.                              *)

Definition Normalizer := forall (Δ : Ctx kind) (κ : kind), typ κ Δ -> typ κ Δ.

Definition nf_sound (nf : Normalizer) : Prop :=
  forall (Δ : Ctx kind) (A B : typ ⋆ Δ),
    nil ⊩ (A ≃ B) -> nf Δ ⋆ A = nf Δ ⋆ B.

Definition nf_separates (nf : Normalizer) : Prop :=
  forall (Δ : Ctx kind) (A B : typ ⋆ Δ),
    ⊮ (A ≃ B) -> nf Δ ⋆ A <> nf Δ ⋆ B.

Lemma Hstar_of_normalizer
  (nf : Normalizer) (Hs : nf_sound nf) (Hd : nf_separates nf) :
  forall (Δ : Ctx kind) (A B : typ ⋆ Δ),
    nil ⊩ (A ≃ B) -> ⊮ (A ≃ B) -> False.
Proof.
  intros Δ A B H HD.
  exact (Hd Δ A B HD (Hs Δ A B H)).
Qed.

(* Key remaining research gap: construct `nf` and prove `nf_sound` and
   `nf_separates`.  In particular, note that Red ⋆ τ = SN τ is far too
   weak for `nf_separates`: distinct constructor heads are all SN.
   The context-indexed hereditary-substitution/total-NBE route is needed
   (or an equivalent semantic model). *)

Definition liftA (κ : kind) {Δ₁ Δ₂ : Ctx kind} (ρ : @Arr kind Δ₁ Δ₂) :

Definition mkShift (κ : kind) (Δ : Ctx kind) : @Arr kind Δ (extC κ Δ) :=

Fixpoint tmap_tmap (κ : kind) (Δ₁ Δ₂ Δ₃ : Ctx kind) (τ : typ κ Δ₁) {struct τ} :
  forall (f : @Arr kind Δ₂ Δ₃) (g : @Arr kind Δ₁ Δ₂),
  tmap f (tmap g τ) = tmap (arrow_comp f g) τ :=
  match τ as τ' in type _ κ' return

From Stdlib Require Import Utf8 List Arith Eqdep_dec Lia Wf_nat
  Wellfounded.Inverse_Image Program.Equality.
Require Import TaskPrefix.
Require Import Lang.FOmegaEq.Types Lang.FOmegaEq.Kinds Lang.FOmegaEq.Syntax
  Lang.FOmegaEq.Typing Lang.FOmegaEq.OpSemantics.
Require Import Binding.Inc Binding.Intrinsic Binding.Lib Binding.Env.
Import Binding.Intrinsic (Ctx, dom, extC, Build_Ctx, mtC).
Import kindEqDec.
Local Open Scope typ_scope.
Local Open Scope bind_scope.

(* ================================================================== *)
(* Normal forms, intrinsically scoped over a context of free names Δ
   with binders represented by context extension extC.  Function-kinded
   normal forms need not be eta-long: nf_neu is allowed at any kind.    *)

Inductive nf (Δ : Ctx kind) : kind -> Type :=
| nf_lam {ka kr : kind} (b : nf (extC ka Δ) kr) : nf Δ (ka ⇒ kr)
| nf_neu {κ : kind} (s : isp Δ κ) : nf Δ κ
| nf_carr (c : ncon Δ) (t : nf Δ ⋆) : nf Δ ⋆
| nf_cprod (c : ncon Δ) (t : nf Δ ⋆) : nf Δ ⋆
with isp (Δ : Ctx kind) : kind -> Type :=
| sp_var {κ : kind} (x : dom Δ) (EQ : Δ x = κ) : isp Δ κ
| sp_ctor {κ : kind} (c : tctor κ) : isp Δ κ
| sp_app {k1 k2 : kind} (s : isp Δ (k1 ⇒ k2)) (a : nf Δ k1) : isp Δ k2
with ncon (Δ : Ctx kind) : Type :=
| ncon_eq (κ : kind) (a b : nf Δ κ) : ncon Δ.

Arguments nf Δ : clear implicits.
Arguments isp Δ : clear implicits.
Arguments ncon Δ : clear implicits.
Arguments nf_lam {Δ ka kr}.
Arguments nf_neu {Δ κ}.
Arguments nf_carr {Δ}.
Arguments nf_cprod {Δ}.
Arguments sp_var {Δ κ}.
Arguments sp_ctor {Δ κ}.
Arguments sp_app {Δ k1 k2}.
Arguments ncon_eq {Δ}.

Scheme nf_mutind := Induction for nf Sort Prop
with isp_mutind := Induction for isp Sort Prop
with ncon_mutind := Induction for ncon Sort Prop.

(* Contexts obtained by adding a list of binders (front-first). *)
Definition ctxL (L : list kind) (Δ : Ctx kind) : Ctx kind :=
  fold_right (fun k Δ => extC k Δ) Δ L.

Lemma ctxL_cons (k : kind) (L : list kind) (Δ : Ctx kind) :
  ctxL (k :: L) Δ = extC k (ctxL L Δ).
Proof. reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma ctxL_app (L1 L2 : list kind) (Δ : Ctx kind) :
  ctxL (L1 ++ L2) Δ = ctxL L1 (ctxL L2 Δ).
Proof.
  induction L1 as [|k L1 IH]; simpl.
  - reflexivity.
  - rewrite IH. reflexivity.
Qed.

(* Canonical embedding of the base context into a context with binders. *)
Fixpoint embL_fun (L : list kind) {Δ : Ctx kind} (x : dom Δ) : dom (ctxL L Δ) :=
  match L with
  | nil => x
  | k :: L' => VS (embL_fun L' x)
  end.

Lemma embL_hom (L : list kind) (Δ : Ctx kind) (x : dom Δ) :
  ctxL L Δ (embL_fun L x) = Δ x.
Proof.
  induction L as [|k L IH]; simpl.
  - reflexivity.
  - exact IH.
Qed.

Definition embL (L : list kind) (Δ : Ctx kind) : @Arr kind Δ (ctxL L Δ) :=
  Build_Arr (embL_fun L) (embL_hom L).

(* Renaming of normal forms along an Arr. *)
Fixpoint rnf {Δ1 Δ2 : Ctx kind} (ρ : @Arr kind Δ1 Δ2)
    {κ : kind} (t : nf Δ1 κ) {struct t} : nf Δ2 κ
with rsp {Δ1 Δ2 : Ctx kind} (ρ : @Arr kind Δ1 Δ2)
    {κ : kind} (s : isp Δ1 κ) {struct s} : isp Δ2 κ
with rncon {Δ1 Δ2 : Ctx kind} (ρ : @Arr kind Δ1 Δ2)
    (c : ncon Δ1) {struct c} : ncon Δ2.
Proof.
  - destruct t as [ka kr b | κ s | c t | c t].
    + exact (@nf_lam Δ2 ka kr (@rnf (extC ka Δ1) (extC ka Δ2) (liftA ka ρ) kr b)).
    + exact (@nf_neu Δ2 κ (@rsp Δ1 Δ2 ρ κ s)).
    + exact (@nf_carr Δ2 (@rncon Δ1 Δ2 ρ c) (@rnf Δ1 Δ2 ρ ⋆ t)).
    + exact (@nf_cprod Δ2 (@rncon Δ1 Δ2 ρ c) (@rnf Δ1 Δ2 ρ ⋆ t)).
  - destruct s as [κ x EQ | κ c | k1 k2 s a].
    + exact (@sp_var Δ2 κ (ρ x) (eq_trans (arr_hom ρ x) EQ)).
    + exact (@sp_ctor Δ2 κ c).
    + exact (@sp_app Δ2 k1 k2 (@rsp Δ1 Δ2 ρ (k1 ⇒ k2) s) (@rnf Δ1 Δ2 ρ k1 a)).
  - destruct c as [κ a b].
    exact (@ncon_eq Δ2 κ (@rnf Δ1 Δ2 ρ κ a) (@rnf Δ1 Δ2 ρ κ b)).
Defined.

Arguments rnf {Δ1 Δ2} ρ {κ} t.
Arguments rsp {Δ1 Δ2} ρ {κ} s.
Arguments rncon {Δ1 Δ2} ρ c.

(* Kind casts. *)
Definition cast_nf {Δ : Ctx kind} {k1 k2 : kind} (e : k1 = k2) (t : nf Δ k1) : nf Δ k2 :=
  match e in (_ = z) return nf Δ z with eq_refl => t end.

Definition cast_sp {Δ : Ctx kind} {k1 k2 : kind} (e : k1 = k2) (s : isp Δ k1) : isp Δ k2 :=
  match e in (_ = z) return isp Δ z with eq_refl => s end.

Definition no_star_arr (k1 k2 : kind) (E : KTyp = KArr k1 k2) : False :=
  match E with end.

(* Codomain reachability for kinds, used to terminate hereditary
   substitution.  kind_cod k k0 holds when k0 is an iterated codomain of k. *)
Inductive kind_cod : kind -> kind -> Type :=
| kc_refl (k : kind) : kind_cod k k
| kc_step {k1 k2 k0 : kind} : kind_cod (k1 ⇒ k2) k0 -> kind_cod k2 k0.

Lemma kind_cod_size {k k0 : kind} (H : kind_cod k k0) : kind_size k <= kind_size k0.
Proof. induction H; [lia | simpl in *; lia]. Qed.

Lemma kind_size_dom_lt (k1 k2 k0 : kind) (H : kind_cod (k1 ⇒ k2) k0) :
  kind_size k1 < kind_size k0.
Proof. pose proof (kind_cod_size H) as Hs. simpl in Hs. lia. Qed.

(* Split a variable of ctxL L (extC k0 Δ) into the distinguished (base)
   variable and an ordinary variable of ctxL L Δ.  None means it is the
   distinguished variable. *)
Fixpoint splitT (L : list kind) (Δ : Ctx kind) (κ0 : kind)
    (x : dom (ctxL L (extC κ0 Δ))) {struct L} : option (dom (ctxL L Δ)) :=
  match L as L0 return dom (ctxL L0 (extC κ0 Δ)) -> option (dom (ctxL L0 Δ)) with
  | nil => fun x => match x with VZ => None | VS y => Some y end
  | k :: L' => fun x =>
      match x with
      | VZ => Some VZ
      | VS y =>
          match splitT L' Δ κ0 y with
          | None => None
          | Some z => Some (VS z)
          end
      end
  end x.

Lemma splitT_none_kind (L : list kind) (Δ : Ctx kind) (κ0 : kind)
    (x : dom (ctxL L (extC κ0 Δ))) :
  splitT L Δ κ0 x = None -> ctxL L (extC κ0 Δ) x = κ0.
Proof.
  revert Δ κ0 x. induction L as [|k L IH]; intros Δ κ0 x E; simpl in *.
  - destruct x; [reflexivity | discriminate E].
  - destruct x as [|y]; [discriminate E|].
    destruct (splitT L Δ κ0 y) eqn:E2; [discriminate E |].
    exact (IH Δ κ0 y eq_refl).
Qed.

Lemma splitT_some_kind (L : list kind) (Δ : Ctx kind) (κ0 : kind)
    (x : dom (ctxL L (extC κ0 Δ))) (y : dom (ctxL L Δ)) :
  splitT L Δ κ0 x = Some y -> ctxL L (extC κ0 Δ) x = ctxL L Δ y.

  revert Δ κ0 x y. induction L as [|k L IH]; intros Δ κ0 x y E; simpl in *.
  - destruct x; [discriminate E |].

      exact (IH Δ κ0 z w E2).

| w_spine {κ : kind} (s : isp (ctxL L Δ) κ) : wres Δ L κ0 κ
| w_target {κ : kind} (v : nf (ctxL L Δ) κ) (H : kind_cod κ κ0) : wres Δ L κ0 κ.

Arguments w_target {Δ L κ0 κ}.

(* ================================================================== *)
(* Evaluation into normal forms, parameterized by an environment of
   normal-form values for the free variables.                           *)

Definition ext_env (Δs Δt : Ctx kind) (ka : kind)
    (env : forall x : dom Δs, nf Δt (Δs x)) :
    forall z : dom (extC ka Δs), nf (extC ka Δt) (extC ka Δs z) :=
  fun z =>
    match z as z0 return nf (extC ka Δt) (extC ka Δs z0) with
    | VZ => @nf_neu (extC ka Δt) ka
              (@sp_var (extC ka Δt) ka VZ eq_refl)
    | VS x => @rnf Δt (extC ka Δt) (@mkShift kind ka Δt) (Δs x) (env x)
    end.

Fixpoint eval (Δs Δt : Ctx kind) (env : forall x : dom Δs, nf Δt (Δs x))
    {κ : kind} (t : typ κ Δs) {struct t} : nf Δt κ :=
  match t as t' in type _ k return nf Δt k with
  | @t_var _ κ x EQ => cast_nf EQ (env x)
  | @t_lam _ ka kr b => nf_lam (eval (extC ka Δs) (extC ka Δt) (ext_env Δs Δt ka env) b)
  | @t_app _ k1 k2 σ τ => appN (eval Δs Δt env σ) (eval Δs Δt env τ)
  | @t_ctor _ κ c => @nf_neu Δt κ (@sp_ctor Δt κ c)
  | @t_carr _ ψ τ => nf_carr (eval_con Δs Δt env ψ) (eval Δs Δt env τ)
  | @t_cprod _ ψ τ => nf_cprod (eval_con Δs Δt env ψ) (eval Δs Δt env τ)
  end
with eval_con (Δs Δt : Ctx kind) (env : forall x : dom Δs, nf Δt (Δs x))
    (ψ : constr Δs) {struct ψ} : ncon Δt :=
  match ψ as ψ' return ncon Δt with
  | @c_eq _ κ a b => @ncon_eq Δt κ (eval Δs Δt env a) (eval Δs Δt env b)
  end.

Arguments eval Δs Δt env {κ} t.
Arguments eval_con Δs Δt env ψ.

Definition idEnv (Δ : Ctx kind) : forall x : dom Δ, nf Δ (Δ x) :=
  fun x => @nf_neu Δ (Δ x) (@sp_var Δ (Δ x) x eq_refl).

Definition norm {Δ : Ctx kind} {κ : kind} (t : typ κ Δ) : nf Δ κ :=
  eval Δ Δ (idEnv Δ) t.
